English

[edit]
English Wikipedia has an article on:
casino (disambiguation)
Wikipedia
English Wikipedia has an article on:
casino (establishment)
Wikipedia

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • cassino (archaic)

Etymology

[edit]

From Italian casino, diminutive form of casa (“house”), from Latin casa (“cottage, hut”).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • (Received Pronunciation) IPA(key): /kəˈsiːnəʊ/
    • Audio (Southern England):(file)
  • (General American, Canada) IPA(key): /kæˈsinoʊ/, /kəˈsinoʊ/
  • (General Australian) IPA(key): /kəˈsiːnəʉ/, /kəˈsiːnɐʉ/
  • (New Zealand) IPA(key): /kəˈsiːnɐʉ/
  • (Indic) IPA(key): /kəˈsino/
  • Rhymes: -iːnəʊ

Noun

[edit]

casino (countable and uncountable, plural casinos or casinoes or casini)

  1. A public building or room for gambling.
    He went to the casino every night till 1:00 am.
    • 2017 August 16, Christopher Knauss, The Guardian:
      A bid by Donald Trump to build Sydney’s first casino was rejected 30 years ago after police expressed concerns about his links to the mafia.
  2. (obsolete) A small house; a pleasure house or holiday home, especially in Italy.
    • 1786 July 3, Hester Thrale Piozzi, Thraliana:
      Quirini [was] knowing in the belles Lettres, & highly skilled in making his Casino comfortable to all the Wits & Blues as we now call them in London.
    • 1792, James Boswell, in Danziger & Brady (eds.), Boswell: The Great Biographer (Journals 1789–1795), Yale 1989, p. 163:
      I felt it strange, and regretted it, that so amiable a man should have contracted such dissolute habits, and at this very time, instead of living respectably with his charming Countess, had Baccelli, the superannuated dancing courtesan, in a casino in the neighbourhood.
  3. (uncountable) A certain Italian card game for two to four players.
  4. (countable) Any of certain cards with special meanings in this game.

Italian

[edit]

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • casinò (casino; place to gamble)

Etymology

[edit]

From casa +‎ -ino; cognate with Piedmontese casin.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /kaˈzi.no/, (traditional) /kaˈsi.no/[1]
  • Rhymes: -ino
  • Hyphenation: ca‧sì‧no

Noun

[edit]

casino m (plural casini)

  1. (colloquial, vulgar) brothel
    Synonym: bordello
  2. (informal, see usage notes) mess
    Ti lascio solo per neanche cinque minuti e mi fai tutto 'sto casino della Madonna?
    I leave you for barely five minutes and you darn messed everything up so much?
  3. (informal, see usage notes) noisy situation
    Synonyms: baccano, confusione, chiasso
    Sì, sì, bellissimo lavorare all'asilo. Vorrei vedertici, a gestire quaranta marmocchi che urlano e fanno casino tutto il giorno
    Yeah, yeah, a real dream working at the kindergarten. I'd like to see you doing it, having to deal with fourty brats screaming around and being loud all day long.
  4. (informal, see usage notes) a large amount, shitload
    Qua c'abbiamo un casino di roba ancora da parte.
    Over here we've got one crapload of stuff still in reserve.
  5. hunting lodge
  6. casino
  7. a particular card game

Usage notes

[edit]

Due to its etymology as a word designating brothels, some consider this to be a swear word or vulgar (typically older people)

Derived terms

[edit]
  • casinista
  • incasinare

[edit]

  • → Ladino: gazino
  • → Ottoman Turkish: قازینو (kazino), غازینو (gazino)
    • Turkish: gazino
  • → Portuguese: casino
  • → Spanish: casino
